overview: The MPS High School Building Committee manages Medford’s participation in the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) core program to renovate or replace the city's aging high school facility. Since its inaugural meeting in May 2024, the committee has overseen project management selection, certified enrollment targets, and conducted exhaustive site and facility investigations. Its work involves balancing a visionary educational plan, including expanded vocational programming, against the technical and financial constraints of the state reimbursement process. As of October 2026, the committee has selected a preferred design schematic and a construction management firm to prepare for a city-wide budget vote scheduled for May 2027.

threads.name: Project Leadership and Procurement
threads.summary: The committee established procurement processes early, forming subcommittees to select an Owner's Project Manager (OPM) and a project designer. After selecting Left Field as the OPM in May 2025, the body moved to evaluate design proposals from multiple firms, ultimately awarding the contract to SMMA in late 2025. In late 2026, the committee concluded a two-phase procurement for a Construction Manager at Risk, voting to enter contract negotiations with Suffolk.

threads.name: Design Alternatives and Option Narrowing
threads.summary: Beginning with 29 conceptual models in early 2026, the committee evaluated a wide range of code upgrades, renovations, and new construction scenarios. This list was narrowed to six finalists in March 2026, which were subjected to rigorous comparative analysis regarding construction phasing, student disruption, and site impact. In June 2026, the committee voted to advance Option C2.2A as the preferred schematic design, citing its cost-effectiveness and preservation of athletic facilities.

threads.name: Educational Programming and Scope
threads.summary: A core objective of the project is expanding Chapter 74 vocational programs and integrating previously isolated services. The committee approved studying nine new or expanded trades, including cybersecurity and plumbing, and reached agreements to co-locate the Curtis Tufts program, the Medford Early Education Program, and a Teen Health Center within the new facility. Space summary reviews in late 2026 focused on aligning these specialized programs with MSBA square footage guidelines.

threads.name: Fiscal Management and Cost Reductions
threads.summary: Following initial estimates that ranged as high as $935 million, the committee initiated a systematic review of 'space efficiencies' to manage the total project cost. Successive rounds of reductions in 2026 targeted administrative offices, classroom sizes, and non-reimbursable areas like the pool basin, resulting in tens of millions in savings. By October 2026, these efforts brought the estimated project cost down to approximately $699 million.

threads.name: Sustainability and Building Systems
threads.summary: The committee established aggressive sustainability goals, targeting LEED certification and compliance with specialized stretch energy codes. After conducting a 50-year life cycle cost analysis comparing geothermal systems with air-source heat pumps, the advisory teams recommended a roof-mounted air-to-water heat pump system. This was finalized alongside a Net Zero energy strategy utilizing solar photovoltaics through a power purchase agreement.

threads.name: Site Challenges and Constraints
threads.summary: Technical investigations revealed significant site obstacles, including an 80-foot grade change, the absence of modern fire protection, and failing mechanical systems in the existing 1970s structure. In 2026, the committee addressed a 1967 deed restriction on portions of the campus, which necessitated the elimination of certain design options and coordination with state environmental agencies. Site planning continues to balance athletic field layouts with parking needs and solar canopy installations.

threads.name: Community Engagement and Communications
threads.summary: To ensure transparency, the committee launched a dedicated project website and established a formal communications plan involving citywide mailers, surveys, and multi-lingual community forums. The committee utilized student-produced videos to document building deficiencies and held specialized breakout sessions on climate and water efficiency. Outreach efforts are timed to milestones such as the narrowing of design options and the upcoming debt exclusion vote.

periods.narrative: The MSBA certified an enrollment projection of 1,395 students while the committee finalized the Request for Services to hire an Owner's Project Manager.
Left Field was hired as the project's OPM, and the committee initiated a peer review of alternative city sites for the new school.
The committee reviewed designer proposals and advanced educational planning through teacher study tours of peer high schools.
SMMA began the feasibility phase, conducting engineering walkthroughs and launching specialized advisory teams for safety, design, and sustainability.
The committee analyzed 29 design alternatives and submitted its Preliminary Design Program to the MSBA after extensive community feedback sessions.
